bull_case: Customers are expanding spend: NRR is above 119%, ARR grew 33%, cloud ARR 39%, and >$100K ARR customers grew 23%. Cyber recovery is mission-critical and broader identity/AI products can deepen wallet share.
bear_case: Direct ROI and CAC payback are not disclosed. High sales-and-marketing intensity and channel concentration could mean customer acquisition is costlier and less proprietary than headline retention suggests.
thesis: Customer pull is strong and improving. Rubrik combines high retention, rising large-customer count and improving contribution margins, which is better evidence than raw revenue growth. The main gap is that direct customer ROI and CAC/payback are not disclosed, so product strength is clear but not 90-level.

evidence.claim: Average subscription dollar-based NRR was above 119% at July 31, 2026.
Subscription ARR reached $1.66B, up 33% y/y; cloud ARR reached $1.48B, up 39%.
Customers with at least $100K of Subscription ARR rose 23% y/y to 3,084.
GAAP gross margin was 78.4% and subscription ARR contribution margin improved to 14.0% from 9.4% a year earlier.
Q2 revenue-normalized-for-material-rights grew 43% y/y, while total revenue grew 38%, reducing the concern that legacy material-right accounting is the main growth driver.

counterevidence: Rubrik does not disclose CAC, sales efficiency, gross retention or cohort payback.
H1 FY2027 sales and marketing expense remained above half of revenue, so acquisition intensity is still high.
Four channel partners represented roughly 26%, 28%, 10% and 10% of Q2 revenue; this is channel concentration even if ultimate customers are diversified.
Agent Cloud-specific retention and willingness-to-pay are not separately disclosed.
unknowns: CAC payback and incremental sales efficiency.
Agent Cloud standalone pricing, ARR and retention.
Ultimate end-customer concentration behind large channel partners.
falsifiers: Cut retention_usage if NRR falls below 110% or large-customer growth falls below 10%.
Cut unit_economics if contribution margin stalls while S&M remains above 50% of revenue.
Escalate dependency risk if one ultimate end customer exceeds 25% of revenue.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: NRR >119%, 33% ARR growth, 23% large-customer growth and improving contribution margin show repeat customer expansion and economic value. High S&M is a risk but does not establish growth without customer value.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Channel concentration is high, but no ultimate end customer >25% is disclosed and the platform spans data, identity, cloud/SaaS and emerging agent security. Fatal single-factor dependence is not demonstrated.

next_checks: Obtain gross retention and cohort churn.
Estimate CAC payback from S&M and net-new ARR.

subscores.rationale: Mission-critical recovery plus >119% NRR supports willingness-to-pay, but direct ROI/payback evidence is insufficient for the 75-90 anchors.
NRR >119%, ARR +33%, cloud ARR +39% and large customers +23% show persistent expansion and increasing wallet share, just below a 90-level multi-year cohort dataset.
78.4% GAAP gross margin and contribution-margin expansion show improving scale economics, but S&M remains high and CAC payback is undisclosed.

uncertainties.rationale: Customer ROI is inferred from retention/expansion rather than disclosed payback data.
NRR is disclosed only as >119%, not an exact quarterly series.
Contribution margin improves but stock-based compensation and acquisition costs complicate owner economics.
